name_reason: Name follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (fd2_animate_scroll_down_in_shop_dialog), accurately reflects the function's job (animate the shop item-list scrolling DOWN), and is symmetric with its counterpart fd2_animate_scroll_up_in_shop_dialog @ 0x2E19B. No Ghidra address residue in the name; 'down' is a direction descriptor, not an ID.
purpose: Animate the shop item-list scrolling DOWN within the mode13h framebuffer region at 0xA8FCA; counterpart of fd2_animate_scroll_up_in_shop_dialog (same shift sizes, reversed direction).
logic_summary: Phase 1: 3 staged shifts of the 0x4A-row block (each row 0x11C bytes, stride 0x140 = mode13h scanline) DOWN by 6 rows (dst 0xA974A = src 0xA8FCA + 6*0x140), iterating row 0x49..0 descending so the overlapping memmove copies high-to-low and does not clobber not-yet-moved source rows; after each shift, clear the top 6 rows to palette 0x49 at 0xA8FCA, then fd2_delay_ms(10). Phase 2: a single final shift of the 0x48-row block DOWN by 8 rows (dst 0xA99CA = src 0xA8FCA + 8*0x140), iterating row 0x47..0 descending, then clear the top 8 rows to palette 0x49 at 0xA8FCA. The __CHK(0x18) stack-probe and the in_stack_* pseudo-vars in the decompile are compiler-generated prologue artifacts, not real parameters.
notes: Source comment block (aniui.c lines 440-471) is already precise and matches the decompile: it documents the backward-iteration overlap reasoning, the +6*0x140 / +8*0x140 destination math, the 0x140 stride, all 5 callers, and the __CHK(0x18) prologue note. No edit needed (comment_verdict=keep). Ghidra plate is consistent with the same understanding (direction, shift sizes, callers, overlap reasoning) so it was left untouched (ghidra_plate_action=none). Decompile confirms void/no-params (param_count=0); only the shard file is added to the working tree, so the source diff is clean. Caller fd2_shop_menu_input_loop invokes this from the Left(0x4B)/Up(0x48) branches when cursor < scroll_offset, i.e. cursor moved above the visible viewport top, matching the comment's 'Up/Left wraps past the visible top'.
